 J&K Bank Opens New Currency Chest Facility In Jammu
 by 
 Observer News Service 
 October 23, 2026 
 J&K Bank Opens New Currency Chest Facility In Jammu 
 Jammu-  Jammu and Kashmir Bank on Friday commissioned a new Currency Chest Building at its Regional Business Centre (RBC) in Jammu, aimed at strengthening currency management infrastructure and ensuring efficient cash distribution across the region.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 The facility was commissioned by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Regional Director Prabhakar Jha and J&K Bank Managing Director and CEO Amitava Chatterjee in the presence of senior officials from both institutions.
 Those present included RBI Deputy General Managers Ram Sarup and Vinod Kumar, J&K Bank General Manager and Divisional Head (Jammu) Ashok Gupta, Deputy General Manager Anup Bhat and Zonal Head (Jammu) Chandrika Parihar.
 Speaking on the occasion, Chatterjee said strengthening currency management infrastructure would improve convenience for customers and support the cash requirements of banks operating in the region.
 “Strengthening our currency management infrastructure is an investment in the convenience of the people we serve,” he said, adding that the facility would help J&K Bank branches and other banks aligned with the currency chest meet customers’ cash requirements.
 He said the infrastructure would strengthen the bank’s capacity to serve households, traders and businesses across the region.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Highlighting the continued importance of physical banking services alongside digital transactions, Chatterjee said dependable access to cash remained essential for many customers and local economic activities.
 “Even as we expand digital banking, dependable access to cash remains essential for many customers and local economic activities,” he said.
 He added that the bank was focused on strengthening both its digital services and physical infrastructure to meet the diverse needs of customers, while acknowledging the RBI’s continued guidance in improving currency management systems and practices.
 RBI Regional Director Prabhakar Jha said efficient currency management was an essential component of public service and played an important role in ensuring the smooth functioning of the banking system.
 He noted that currency chests help maintain the availability of banknotes and coins and facilitate the withdrawal of soiled notes from circulation.

 Jha said strengthening such infrastructure supported the banking system’s ability to meet the currency requirements of the public.
 He also emphasised the importance of sound operational controls, adherence to prescribed procedures and coordination among banks to ensure secure and efficient currency distribution. The commissioning of the facility marks another step in J&K Bank’s efforts to strengthen the infrastructure supporting its service network and contribute to the region’s banking and economic activities.
